strategy.summary: Reproduce PR #22973 by building SciPy from source at buggy commit a011b598d923 with the reported toolchain, then run the developer's test_issue_22704 in scipy/interpolate/tests/test_bsplines.py. The test expects ValueError from make_splrep(x, y, w=w, k=2, s=12) on the 18-point dataset with constant weights 1.38723. On the buggy revision the call raises BSplineFitException (internal error) instead, so the assertion fails. On the fixed revision the NaN residual check raises ValueError and the test passes. The pip-installed scipy==1.15.2 wheel is not the buggy source and must not be used for the transition.

If BSplineFitException subclasses ValueError on the buggy revision, assert_raises(ValueError) would pass on buggy and the transition would not occur. Confirm the class hierarchy before relying on the failure.
The expected exception class is ambiguous in the evidence: a RuntimeError appears in an earlier diff, while the final commit and the added test use ValueError. The test as written asserts ValueError.
The s threshold (s=9.6) is only an example and not an established boundary; the test uses s=12.
numpy version is not documented as required; 1.26.4 is chosen from the issue environment and may need to be changed if the build fails against the buggy source.
The buggy commit date (PR DATE) is not given, and the link between a011b598d923 and the failing behaviour is not established beyond the header.
No ULP or tolerance threshold applies; the atol=5e-13 in test_s_too_small belongs to a different test and must not be assumed here.
Building SciPy from source needs a working Fortran and C/C++ toolchain; a mismatch with the reported gfortran 13.3.0 or clang 15.0.0 could prevent the build.

oracle.why: The oracle is an exception type check (ValueError), not a numeric comparison, so no numeric tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: make_splrep raises BSplineFitException (internal error) because coefficients become NaN in back substitution; assert_raises(ValueError) does not catch it, so the test errors.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The residuals.sum() NaN check raises ValueError with the _iermesg[1] message, which assert_raises(ValueError) catches, so the test passes.
